However, the device with barrier film is observed to be more stable under maximum power point tracking, retaining ~72% of its initial PCE after 220h, as compared to ~64% PCE retention for the control device. This is a surprising result, and we hypothesize that either the thickness of the film is preventing or increasing the water or atmospheric diffusion path length or that the phosphates present in the lead barrier are minorly passivating the perovskite layer in the device itself. In Final Update I to the Third Edition of the Test Methods for Evaluating Solid Waste, Physical/Chemical Methods; 1992. In order to determine the total lead concentration, we performed microwave digestion to dissolve the lead and then analyzed the lead concentration of the resulting solution with inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES). The same devices that underwent the maximum power point tracking in Figure 9.1(c), (d) were used to perform the TCLP (Milestone 1.3.2). As shown in Figure 9.2(a), the aged device with the barrier film had a leached Pb content of 3.33±0.87 mg L-1, under the U.S. EPA Pb limit of 5 mg L-1. On the other hand, the control device without barrier film had a leached Pb content of 8.95±1.23 mg L-1, failing the U.S. EPA limit. Note also that the devices underwent over 200 h of maximum power point tracking, which is twice over the stated 100 h goal of milestone 1.3.2. Figure 9.2. The ideal chemical barrier film for perovskite solar cells should be robust and able to effectively capture and contain Pb even after significant weathering. We then aged our devices with barrier film to the damp heat double 85°C/85% relative humidity (RH) test for 50 h in the dark. These devices utilized our new dopant-free spiro-MeOTAD at the hole-transporting layer. As shown in Figure 9.2(a), the aged device with the barrier film had a leached Pb content of 2.71±0.92 mg L-1, therefore meeting the U.S. EPA Pb limit of 5 mg L-1 (Milestone 1.3.3, GNG- 2E). In summary, the results presented in Figure 9.2 collectively fulfill Milestone 1.3.2, 1.3.3, GNG-2E, and EOP-C.
